candidate_spec.high_level_variant: Town01 mission with same general start–end corridor but slightly different spawn and destination, drier but still wet conditions, and minimally adjusted puddles; ego approaches an intersection governed by multiple lights including red states, with zero vehicle_cmd yet nonzero ego motion, again triggering a red-light oracle event while collision remains optional.
candidate_spec.mutation_intent: Probe whether the red-light violation with zero commands and nonzero motion persists under slightly reduced rain/puddle intensity and a modestly altered route geometry, while keeping traffic-light complexity and unknown route–light relation intact.
pre_execution_validation_rules: Ensure the scenario runs on Town01 with only the ego as a dynamic actor.
Verify that traffic_lights topics are active and include multiple distinct signals along the ego path.
Confirm at least one traffic light reports a red phase during the time interval when the ego approaches an intersection.
Check that final_waypoints remain nonempty (waypoint count > 0) from mid-route through the anticipated intersection region.
Ensure weather, wetness, and puddle settings remain within moderate bounds so visibility and physics are plausible but not extreme.
post_execution_validation_rules: Verify the oracle reports a red-light violation; do not enforce lane_invasion=1 as a requirement.
Confirm that traffic_lights logs show at least one active red state shortly before or during the time the oracle flags the violation.
Check that final_waypoints are still being published and nonempty in the frames just before the violation timestamp.
Confirm vehicle_cmd remains effectively zero (no significant steering, throttle, or brake command) while vehicle_status shows nonzero ego speed during the violation window.
Record any collision messages and their impulses but treat collision as optional, not mandatory, for matching this case.
Do not attempt to infer which specific light governs the ego or whether a stop line is physically crossed unless future logs explicitly provide that association.
uncertainty: Whether the ego truly crosses a governing red light’s stop line is not guaranteed by traffic_lights data and remains uncertain.
Lane invasion behavior may or may not occur; validation must not rely on it because of prior label conflicts.
The severity and relevance of any collisions to the underlying bug are uncertain given prior crash=false flags.
Without internal module traces, it will remain unclear whether the zero-command/nonzero-motion pattern reflects planning, control, simulator, or logging anomalies.
